advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the bug-tier precheck branch, honor P8-too-big (short-circuit run_llm=False, or otherwise avoid feeding an oversized bug plan into the LLM finder tier).
evidence: workflow_ops.py:166-178 bug branch returns `det_blocking: []` and `run_llm: True` with no P8 check

The non-bug path guards this: workflow_ops.py:199-202 `p8_too_big = any(getattr(r,'id',None)=='P8' and getattr(r,'blocked',False) ...)` then `if p8_too_big: ... return {**base, 'run_llm': False, 'verdict': verdict}`
det_floor.py:591-608 P8 emits a blocking too-big finding when `plan_tokens > budget`

sizing.py:255-284 the single-turn leaf ladder attempts model calls (`continue  # context limit at this model → escalate to the next`) before producing the `_too_big` failure finding — i.e. real LLM calls are made before giving up
workflow_ops.py:176 `"run_llm": True` set for every bug regardless of routing
criteria_routing.json:1217-1221 `necessity` `applies_at.scope: ["leaf"]` — it does not apply to a container
orchestrator.route_criteria (orchestrator.py:355-388) will yield no criteria for a container bug since necessity is the only BUG_TIER_CRITERIA and it is filtered by applies() scope
advisory.finding: The bug-tier precheck path sets run_llm=True and det_blocking=[] unconditionally, bypassing the P8-too-big deterministic short-circuit that the non-bug path applies. A bug with an oversized plan (plan tokens > the largest context window) now flows into the LLM finder tier instead of short-circuiting; for a leaf plan the single-turn size ladder actually issues model calls and catches context-limit errors before emitting a _too_big finding, incurring the wasted LLM cost the P8 gate exists to prevent. Pre-R4 such a bug never ran any LLM at all.
merged_from: The bug tier always sets run_llm=True, but the sole bug-tier criterion `necessity` has applies_at.scope=["leaf"], so a bug that is a container (has children) routes zero LLM criteria while still triggering the LLM finder tier with an empty included set.
scenarios: A bug ticket whose plan/description exceeds the largest model context window is submitted to the gate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse the existing p8_too_big detection in the bug branch: if the DET floor reports P8 blocked, return run_llm=False with a non-blocking (advisory) too-big disposition rather than routing into the LLM tier.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a bug-tier test using a DET-blocking plan (e.g. no `## Acceptance Criteria`, which fires P1) and assert precheck yields `det_blocking == []`, the block appears in `det_advisory`, and the terminal verdict is PASS (not BLOCK).
evidence: workflow_ops.py:167-174: `det_blocks = det_floor.det_blocking_findings(...)` ... `"det_blocking": [],  # a bug is never blocked` / `"det_advisory": [*det_blocks, *det_advisories]` — the downgrade of a would-be-blocking DET finding to advisory

tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py:34-39: `_BUG_DESC` contains `## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] Y no longer happens...` — a well-formed plan that fires no P1 DET block, so `test_precheck_bug_runs_light_tier_never_blocking` asserts `out["det_blocking"] == []` on input that had no blocking DET findings to downgrade

tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_workflow.py:452-463: the sibling `test_p1_det_block_still_runs_llm_and_blocks` shows a plan with NO `## Acceptance Criteria` produces `verdict == "BLOCK"` for a non-bug — the exact plan shape whose bug-tier downgrade to PASS is left untested
ABSENCE: no bug-tier test constructs a bug plan that produces a DET block (e.g. missing acceptance criteria → P1) and asserts it is downgraded to advisory + PASSes rather than BLOCKs
advisory.finding: The bug tier's load-bearing safety guarantee — that a bug is NEVER blocked even when the DET floor produces a would-be-blocking finding (precheck downgrades det_blocks into det_advisory and forces det_blocking=[]) — is never exercised. Every bug-tier test uses a well-formed plan that produces NO blocking DET finding, so `det_blocking == []` / `blocking == []` is asserted only in the trivial no-block case; the downgrade code path (workflow_ops.py:167-174) never runs.
scenarios: A future edit regresses `det_blocking=[]` to pass `det_blocks` through (or the downgrade merge into det_advisory is dropped) — a bug would then block, contradicting the stated 'never blocks a bug' contract, and no unit test would fail.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that patches reads with a bug whose description omits `## Acceptance Criteria` (mirroring test_p1_det_block_still_runs_llm_and_blocks), then assert `out['det_blocking'] == []`, that the P1 finding is present in `out['det_advisory']`, and end-to-end the verdict is PASS with `blocking == []`.
